source_text: Στίχ. α΄. Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωϋσῆν. Ἐν ὅλαις τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέραις δοῦναι τὸν νόμον κατεῖχε τὸν Μωῦσῆν (11) ὁ πάνσοφος Θεὸς, καίτοι δυνατῶς ἔχων ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις δοῦναι τὸν Νόμον. Ἀλλʼ ἵνα τὸ κεκρυμμένον τῆς ἀσεβείας ἐν τῷ βάθει τῆς καρδίας τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἀπουσίας Μωῦσέως ἐλέγξῃ.
thought_title: Why God kept Moses forty days
orientation: Origen is commenting on Exodus 31:1, explaining why God kept Moses on the mountain for forty days before giving the law.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 1. And the Lord spoke to Moses. For whole forty days, to give the law, the all-wise God held Moses, although being able in three days to give the law. But in order that the hidden impiety in the depth of the heart of the Jews the time of the absence of Moses might expose.

choices.why: The adjective 'whole' emphasizes the complete duration of the forty days, matching the source's emphasis on the full period.
The verb means to hold back or detain; 'held' preserves the sense of God keeping Moses on the mountain.
The compound adjective means 'all-wise'; rendering it as a single adjective preserves the source's emphasis on God's complete wisdom.
The participle 'hidden' is used substantivally with the genitive 'of impiety'; this rendering keeps the noun phrase structure clear.
The verb means to convict, refute, or expose; 'expose' fits the context of revealing hidden impiety.

pass_b_english: And the Lord spoke to Moses (Exodus 31:1). The all-wise God held Moses for whole forty days to give the law, although he was fully able to give the law in three days. But he did this so that the time of Moses' absence might expose the hidden impiety in the depth of the Jews' hearts.

problems.quote: held Moses for whole forty days
problems.why: 'Held' suggests detained against will; context suggests God kept/retained Moses purposefully.

problems.quote: the hidden impiety in the depth of the Jews' heart
problems.why: Anachronistic 'Jews' for Israelites at Sinai; also 'depth' singular with 'Jews' plural.
problems.fix: 'the Israelites' hearts' or note on Origen's usage.

fixed: Changed 'held' to 'kept' to reflect purposeful retention, not detention against will.
Changed 'heart' to 'hearts' to agree with plural 'Jews'; kept 'Jews' as the source uses 'τῶν Ἰουδαίων' and the work brief lists 'Jews' as the cast name.
